# Rewrite `intropy run` for the reworked topology schema

## Context

The `.NET Intropy.Topology` generator now emits `.intropy/topology.json` in a new,
flatter format (`apiVersion: topology.intropy.io/v1`) — this is the "Go
reader/dashboard sync" that memory noted as deferred. The reference structure is
`~/dev/intropy/customers/fluxia/integrations/domains/price/distribution/.intropy/topology.json`.

`intropy run` starts a read-only dashboard (`internal/dashboard.Serve`) whose Flow
view renders a system's declared topology. The current Go parser
(`internal/topology`) and the React graph builder (`FlowView.tsx`) both understand
only the **old** schema (integer `schemaVersion`, `system` object, `resources[]`,
flat `edges[]`). Loaded against a v1 record the Go parser fails with
"unsupported schema version 0". This change re-points the reader and the flow
canvas at v1 so the dashboard renders the new records.

### What the new schema looks like (vs. old)

| | Old | New (v1) |
|---|---|---|
| version | `schemaVersion: 1` (int) | `apiVersion: "topology.intropy.io/v1"` + `kind: "SystemTopology"` |
| system | object `{name,owner,domain}` | bare string (`"distribution"`) |
| wiring | one flat `edges[]` list of `<kind>:<name>` refs | **inlined per component**: `subscribes[]`, `publishes[]`, `provides[]`, `consumes[]`, `connectors[]` |
| infra | `resources[]` (topics + connectors mixed) | top-level `topics[]` and `connectors[]` sections |
| component→project join | explicit `project` field | component `name` == subdirectory name |
| dropped | `generator`, component `tags`/`workload`/`trigger`/`project` | — |

Decisions (confirmed with user): **new schema only** — old-schema files become
`List()` warnings, not fatal. **Topics + connectors rendered now**; `provides`/
`consumes`/`apis` are parsed but not rendered (all empty in the sample) — rendered
later when the API contract-surface shape is known.

## Blast radius (confirmed)

Only two Go files reference `internal/topology` (`handlers.go`, `api.ts`), and
`handlers.go` uses just `topology.List`/`topology.Entry` — it never touches the
struct fields, so **the new struct shape flows through it with no code change**.
The command wiring (`cmd/intropy/int_run.go`, `internal/dashboard/server.go`,
`static.go`, `browser.go`) is schema-agnostic and unchanged.

## Changes

### 1. `internal/topology/topology.go` — rewrite structs + `Load`

Replace the old types with v1. Keep `RelPath`, `List`, `listSkipDirs`, and `Entry`
(still `{ Path string; Topology }`) exactly as-is — only the embedded shape changes.

```go
const (
    APIVersion = "topology.intropy.io/v1"
    Kind       = "SystemTopology"
    RelPath    = ".intropy/topology.json"
)

type Topology struct {
    APIVersion string      `json:"apiVersion"`
    Kind       string      `json:"kind"`
    System     string      `json:"system"`
    Components []Component `json:"components,omitempty"`
    Topics     []Topic     `json:"topics,omitempty"`
    Connectors []Connector `json:"connectors,omitempty"`
    // Deferred: element shape not yet finalized. Parsed opaquely so records
    // round-trip to the frontend without asserting a schema we don't render.
    APIs []json.RawMessage `json:"apis,omitempty"`
}

type Component struct {
    Name       string            `json:"name"`
    Kind       string            `json:"kind"`
    Subscribes []TopicRef        `json:"subscribes,omitempty"`
    Publishes  []Publication     `json:"publishes,omitempty"`
    Connectors []ConnectorUse    `json:"connectors,omitempty"`
    Provides   []json.RawMessage `json:"provides,omitempty"` // deferred
    Consumes   []json.RawMessage `json:"consumes,omitempty"` // deferred
}

type TopicRef     struct { PubSub, Topic string }               // subscribes[]
type Publication  struct { Port, PubSub, Topic string }         // publishes[] (Port omitempty)
type ConnectorUse struct { Connector, Direction string }        // component.connectors[] ("in"|"out")
type Topic        struct { PubSub, Topic, Contract string; Publishers, Subscribers []string }
type Transport    struct { Type string; SupportsInput, SupportsOutput bool }
type Connector    struct { Name, ExternalSystem string; Transport Transport; Directions, UsedBy []string }
```
(JSON tags as in the sample: `pubsub`, `topic`, `port`, `contract`, `externalSystem`,
`transport`, `supportsInput`, `supportsOutput`, `directions`, `usedBy`, etc.)

`Load`: validate `apiVersion` (and reject unknown values — the same
"error, not a guess" philosophy the old version-check had):
```go
if t.APIVersion != APIVersion {
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("topology record %s: unsupported apiVersion %q (this CLI understands %q)",
        path, t.APIVersion, APIVersion)
}
```
`List` is unchanged — a v0/old-schema record now fails `Load` (empty `apiVersion`)
and is surfaced as a warning while still counting as a system root, exactly the
existing malformed-record behavior.

### 2. `internal/topology/topology_test.go` — rewrite fixtures

Replace `validRecord` with a v1 body (model it on the price sample). Update
assertions: `System` is a string; assert `Topics`/`Connectors`/`Publishes`/
`Connectors[].Direction`; rename `TestLoadUnsupportedVersion` to assert the
`unsupported apiVersion` message (feed a `{"apiVersion":"topology.intropy.io/v99"}`
body). `List` tests keep their structure but reference `entry.System` (string).

### 3. `internal/dashboard/handlers.go` — no change

Verified: `topologies` only calls `topology.List` and rewrites `Entry.Path`. The
served JSON shape changes automatically from the new embedded struct.

### 4. `web/src/api.ts` — rewrite the Topology TS interfaces

Mirror the Go structs. `system` becomes `string`. Add `Topic`, `Connector`,
`Transport`, `Publication`, `TopicRef`, `ConnectorUse`; type `provides`/`consumes`/
`apis` as `unknown[]` (deferred). Drop `TopologyResource`, `TopologyEdge`,
`TopologyApi`, `generator`, `schemaVersion`, `TopologyTrigger`. Keep the `path`
field (server-injected root-relative id). The API client functions
(`api.topologies` etc.) are unchanged.

### 5. `web/src/components/FlowView.tsx` — rewrite the declared-graph builder

Reuse unchanged: all layout constants, the `place`/longest-path (Kahn) column
layering, `topologyFor` (path-containment match still valid), `TEMPLATE_DATA_FLOW`,
`refName`, and every node component (`GroupNode`, `IntegrationNode`, `TopicNode`,
`ExternalNode`, `InfraNode`) + `NODE_TYPES`. Only the data-derivation inside
`buildDeclaredGraph` and two small call sites change.

- **System label** (line ~190): `g.opt.label = t.system` (was `t.system.name`);
  group node title `topo.system` (was `topo.system.name`).
- **`buildDeclaredGraph(topo, items)`** — derive the graph from component inline
  edges instead of the flat `edges[]`:
  - **Component→integration join by name** (replaces `project`): candidate path
    `joinProject(topo.path, c.name)`; if it matches an `items` entry, the node id
    is that path (clickable → selects the integration), else `component:<name>`.
    Reuse the existing `joinProject` helper.
  - **Topic nodes**: collect the unique `{pubsub,topic}` set referenced by every
    component's `publishes`+`subscribes`; look up `contract` from `topo.topics`
    (keyed by `pubsub/topic`). Node id `topic:<pubsub>/<topic>`. `TopicNode` shows
    entity/contract as today (entity is gone from v1 → show topic name + contract).
  - **Edges**: for each component, one edge per `publishes` (component→topic, keep
    `port` as label metadata), per `subscribes` (topic→component), and per
    `connectors` entry — `direction:"in"` = external→component (source, placed
    left), `direction:"out"` = component→external (sink, placed below), reusing the
    existing `pushExternal`/`belowY`/`centerUnder` anchoring.
  - **External nodes**: from component `connectors[]`; enrich name/type from
    `topo.connectors` lookup by `connector` name — display name
    `externalSystem` (via `refName`) falling back to the connector name, type
    `transport.type` (now an object, was a string).
  - **Column layering**: run the existing longest-path relaxation over the derived
    component↔topic edge set (build `succ`/`indeg` from the publish/subscribe
    edges); connectors/externals stay off the internal layering as today.
  - **dataFlow badge**: `TEMPLATE_DATA_FLOW[c.kind]`. Make the lookup
    case-insensitive (or add `transactionalintegration`/`transactionalintegration`)
    so `kind: "transactionalIntegration"` resolves to `both`. Trigger badge is
    dropped (no `trigger` in v1) — leave `IntNodeData.trigger` unset.

`buildGraph` (the no-topology Dapr-YAML fallback) is untouched.

### 6. Rebuild the embedded SPA

`web/dist` is embedded via `//go:embed` and the built assets are committed. After
the TS edits, run `make web` (`npm ci && npm run build`) to regenerate
`web/dist/assets/*` so the binary serves the updated canvas.

## Verification

1. **Go**: `go test ./internal/topology/... ./internal/dashboard/... ./cmd/...`
2. **Web typecheck + build**: `cd web && npm run typecheck && npm run build`
   (or `make web`).
3. **API shape**: `go run ./cmd/intropy int run ~/dev/intropy/customers/fluxia/integrations/domains/price --no-browser`
   then `curl -s localhost:8730/api/topology | jq` — expect one entry,
   `system:"distribution"`, 4 components, 2 topics, 4 connectors, `path:"distribution"`.
4. **End-to-end canvas** (chrome-devtools MCP or a browser): open the dashboard,
   Flow view, select the **distribution** system. Expect: `extractor` publishing to
   `price-b2b` + `price-b2c` topics; `erp-loader` subscribing `price-b2b`;
   `wms-loader` subscribing `price-b2c`; `price-master` (sftp, `in`) as a source
   into `extractor` and `web-integration`; `erp`/`wms`/`trading-partner` as `out`
   sinks. Clicking a component card selects its integration in the sidebar.
5. **Regression**: confirm an old-schema dir (e.g. `product/distribution`) no longer
   renders a declared graph but does **not** crash the canvas — it falls back to the
   heuristic `buildGraph` and `/api/topology` simply omits it (with a server-side
   warning), per the new-schema-only decision.

Yes — it's genuinely easy, because the dashboard is already built for it. Every color is a CSS variable with a light default (`:root`) and a dark override, and the only theme-aware JS is React Flow's `colorMode`. Right now it just follows the OS (`@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` + `colorMode="system"`) with no manual control.

Adding a toggle is three small edits:

1. **`index.css`** — make the dark palette also apply via `:root[data-theme="dark"]`, and add a `:root[data-theme="light"]` block so an explicit choice overrides the OS in both directions (the media query stays as the default when no choice is made). ~15 lines, mechanical.
2. **`App.tsx`** — a tiny theme hook: initialize from `localStorage` (falling back to system), write `document.documentElement.dataset.theme`, and a sun/moon button in the topbar next to the version chip. Mirrors the existing `SIDEBAR_COLLAPSED_KEY` persistence pattern already there.
3. **`FlowView.tsx`** — pass the resolved theme to `colorMode` instead of the hardcoded `"system"` so the canvas chrome (controls, minimap, edges) follows the toggle.

Then rebuild the SPA (`make web`). Maybe 20–30 minutes including a visual check.

Done — the dashboard now has a working 3-state theme toggle. It was easy precisely because the design was already fully variable-driven.

## What I added

- **`web/index.html`** — a tiny inline script that resolves the theme (`localStorage` preference, falling back to the OS) and sets `data-theme` on `<html>` *before first paint*, so there's no flash.
- **`web/src/index.css`** — replaced the `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block with `:root[data-theme="dark"]` / `[data-theme="light"]` rules (including `color-scheme`). Since "system" is resolved to a concrete value in JS, the CSS stays simple with no duplicated palette. Added `.theme-toggle` + `.topbar-end` styling.
- **`web/src/App.tsx`** — a `ThemePref` state (`light` → `dark` → `system`) persisted to `localStorage` under `intropy.theme`, an effect that applies `data-theme` and (in system mode) live-follows OS changes via `matchMedia`, and a `ThemeToggle` button in the top bar that cycles the mode with a matching sun/moon/auto glyph and an accessible label.
- **`web/src/components/FlowView.tsx`** — takes a resolved `theme` prop and passes it to React Flow's `colorMode` (was hardcoded `"system"`), so the canvas chrome follows the toggle.
- **`web/src/icons.ts`** — added `LightModeIcon`, `DarkModeIcon`, `SystemThemeIcon`.

## Verified
`npm run build` clean; in the browser the button reads "Theme: System", cycles to light instantly across the whole UI (including the Flow canvas), and the icon updates per state. SPA bundle rebuilt into `web/dist` (embedded in the binary).
